name: Deerhunter
label: 4AD
lede: Bradford Cox took a band name he hated, a friend's death and a failed session in a Brooklyn studio and turned Atlanta's weirdest punk band into one of the most loved indie groups of its decade, while the internet leaked nearly everything before he could release it.

eras.title: A name he hated, a friend he lost
eras.text: Deerhunter started in Atlanta as what Bradford Cox thought was a throwaway art project. It turned into a band just as its bassist died, and the first album came out of that grief.

years.h: Bradford Cox and Moses Archuleta start Deerhunter in Atlanta
years.p: First drummer Dan Walton names the band. Cox, born with Marfan syndrome and living alone in a suburban house as a teenager after his parents divorced, later says he hated the name.
years.xp: Cox met guitarist Colin Mee at Die Slaughterhaus Records, and they bonded over Dada, Messiaen, Ligeti, [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]], [[The Raincoats|42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600]] and Cabaret Voltaire. Paul Harper played bass first; Justin Bosworth replaced him.

years.h: Bassist Justin Bosworth dies after a skateboarding accident
years.p: Bosworth dies at 24 from head injuries. His only release with Deerhunter is a split EP with Alphabets, and the debut album's liner notes are dedicated to him.

q: I don't ever want to make this album again.
years.h: Turn It Up Faggot on Stickfigure, made out of grief
years.p: Josh Fauver of Electrosleep International joins on bass for the debut. Bradford Cox calls it the result of a lot of negativity.

years.h: Lockett Pundt, Bradford Cox's childhood friend, joins
years.p: Pundt comes in as second guitarist, songwriting partner and occasional lead singer.

years.h: The Rare Book Room sessions collapse
years.p: Deerhunter's first try at a second album, in Brooklyn with Samara Lubelski, falls apart: Bradford Cox has influenza and walking pneumonia, the piano is out of tune and the tape machine uncalibrated.
years.xp: Cox said he kept the failed sessions on a scratched CD-R under his bed that nobody would ever hear. Excerpts later went up as free downloads on the band's blog anyway.

eras.title: The Kranky years, leaked
eras.text: Two records on Chicago's Kranky made Deerhunter a critics' band and Bradford Cox a compulsive, oversharing blogger. Fans got his music early whether he wanted them to or not.

years.h: Cryptograms on Kranky: Pitchfork Best New Music
years.p: Cut in rural Georgia over two single-day sessions, the first ending as "Red Ink" spins the tape off the reel. It's dedicated to Bradley Ira Harris, a heroin-addicted friend of Bradford Cox's who died in 2005.
years.xp: Chris Bishop produced and engineered, at the same studio as the debut. The second half was recorded months later in one day in November. Pitchfork named it its 14th best album of 2007.

years.h: Fluorescent Grey EP
years.p: Deerhunter adds rudimentary keyboards, bells and piano on the Kranky EP.

years.h: Colin Mee quits over missed shows, then comes back
years.p: Mee says he couldn't make a couple of booked shows and certain bandmates found that unacceptable. He's back four months later.

q: I did not react well to the leak, in retrospect.
years.h: Bradford Cox's Atlas Sound album Logos leaks
years.p: An unfinished version of Cox's solo record leaks online. Microcastle had leaked in May too.

years.h: Microcastle, with Weird Era Cont. made because of the leak
years.p: Recorded in a week at Rare Book Room with Nicolas Vernhes. Kranky rushes it out digitally on August 19 after the leak, and the band records a bonus album, which leaks too.
years.xp: Microcastle is Deerhunter's first entry on the Billboard 200, at No. 123, and Wikipedia says it sold over 50,000 copies in the US. Lockett Pundt wrote "Agoraphobia," and [[Black Lips|e940d7a3-01d0-468c-86ea-5dc4d89dcf80]]' Cole Alexander added vocals to "Saved by Old Times" over iChat. Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and ranked it fifth of 2008.

years.h: Colin Mee leaves for good; Whitney Petty joins
years.p: Petty, a former cheerleader and high-school friend of Bradford Cox, takes the second guitar slot for tours.

years.h: Whitney Petty is out; Deerhunter is a four-piece again
years.p: Bradford Cox announces the change and says Deerhunter is the four of them.

years.h: Rainwater Cassette Exchange EP
years.p: Songs written during the Microcastle sessions. That summer Deerhunter tours as the No Deachunter Tour with [[No Age|55821c25-bd47-4f67-baf8-17ccd2cf1c86]] and [[Dan Deacon|8dd73d1a-0424-4581-af8c-ade3edb44c5a]].

years.h: At ATP, Bradford Cox announces a hiatus
years.p: At the Flaming Lips-curated All Tomorrow's Parties, Cox says it's the last show for a long time. Moses Archuleta enrolls in culinary school.

eras.title: Halcyon days on 4AD
eras.text: The hiatus lasted months, not years. Deerhunter moved to 4AD and made the album most people now name first, then lost a founding bassist by email.

years.h: Halcyon Digest on 4AD: Pitchfork's No. 3 album of 2010
years.p: Launched with a guerrilla campaign and "Revival" given to fans who helped promote it. AllMusic gives five stars; Pitchfork later ranks it 29th of the 2010s.
years.xp: The saxophone on "Coronado" came from Bradford Cox playing the Rolling Stones' Exile on Main St. reissue on repeat. He predicted everyone would have saxophones on their records the next year.

years.h: Josh Fauver quits Deerhunter by email
years.p: Fauver leaves just before the Monomania sessions. Josh McKay takes bass and Atlanta's Frankie Broyles joins on guitar.

years.h: "Monomania" on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon
years.p: Deerhunter plays the title track on network TV a month before release.

years.h: Monomania: nocturnal garage with rats on tape
years.p: Recorded at Rare Book Room with Nicolas Vernhes, it uses treated recordings of rats and insects and deals with dissociation and mental illness.

years.h: Deerhunter curates ATP and plays three albums in full
years.p: At Pontins holiday camp in Camber Sands, Deerhunter headlines and curates the weekend, playing Cryptograms, Microcastle and Halcyon Digest start to finish. Atlas Sound plays too.

eras.title: Hit by a car, then a slow fade
eras.text: A car hit Bradford Cox while he was walking his dog, and the recovery produced the band's warmest record. Four years later a former bassist died, and after one more album Deerhunter stopped.

years.big: Walking the dog in Grant Park. Then the hospital.
years.h: Bradford Cox is hit by a car in Atlanta
years.p: Cox is seriously injured and hospitalized after a vehicle hits him while he walks his dog near Grant Park. He writes songs through his rehabilitation.

years.h: Fading Frontier, written in recovery
years.p: Preceded by "Snakeskin," with saxophonist Zumi Rosow in its video, and "Living My Life," dedicated to Miles Davis.

years.h: Double Dream of Spring, a tour-only cassette
years.p: A mostly instrumental album sold only on cassette on tour.

years.h: Former bassist Josh Fauver dies at 39
years.p: Deerhunter announces that Fauver has died in Atlanta. No cause of death was announced.

years.h: Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared? with Cate Le Bon
years.p: Produced by Cate Le Bon. The single "Death in Midsummer" came out the previous October.

years.h: "Timebends": 13 minutes, one take, straight to tape
years.p: A partly improvised Halloween single recorded live with almost no overdubs. After a European tour that November, Deerhunter goes quiet.

eras.title: Eight new songs in Philadelphia
eras.text: Deerhunter has been inactive since 2019. In 2026 Bradford Cox came back onstage alone.

years.h: Bradford Cox plays eight new songs at Making Time, Philadelphia
years.p: After years of near-silence, Cox performs at Philadelphia's Making Time Festival with eight new songs.
